title: What living things are made of
question: What kinds of molecules do living things build and use?
hook: Just four elements make up 96% of a human body's mass.
idea: Biomolecules range from small vitamins to huge chains, and a few big families cover most of the large ones.

beats.explain: Proteins, carbohydrates, lipids and nucleic acids are the large macromolecules; vitamins and hormones are small molecules.

beats.prompt: Match each sugar to its type
beats.explain: Monosaccharides are single sugars, disaccharides join two, and polysaccharides are polymerized monosaccharides.

beats.prompt: A cell builds a new RNA strand. Where DNA would use thymine, which base does RNA use?

choices.label: Adenine
choices.feedback: Adenine is used by both DNA and RNA, so it cannot be the swap.

choices.label: Cytosine
choices.feedback: Cytosine appears in both DNA and RNA too.

beats.explain: DNA uses C, G, A and T, while RNA uses C, G, A and U.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: A biomolecule is a molecule produced by a living organism.
Many biomolecules are endogenous, meaning produced within the organism.
Nutrients taken in from food are exogenous biomolecules.
So an organism can survive entirely on what it makes itself.
beats.explain: Organisms usually also need exogenous biomolecules, such as certain nutrients, to survive.
